_note: Two things that cannot come out of the headers mechanically.
`sub` holds corrections to harvested examples, from compiling all of them
with MSVC against the real headers at /std:c++20. Each entry says what the
compiler said, so a stale fixup can be recognised as stale. gen.pl reports
any entry that matches nothing, so this file cannot rot silently.
`messages` holds the script lifecycle callbacks. ScriptBehaviour
DELIBERATELY does not declare them - that absence is the whole mechanism,
because it is what lets the compiler tell which ones you actually wrote.
So there is no declaration to copy, and they are written out here instead.
Each one carries the line of the concept in ScriptHooks.h that detects it,
which is the closest thing to a declaration they have.

sub.why: C2100: you cannot dereference an operand of type 'eng::NameHandle'. NameHandle has a std::formatter, so it is passed as `name`, not `*name`.
A bare expression is not a statement; shown as the declaration a caller would actually write.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnStart
ScriptBehaviour.summary: Once, on the first update of either kind after this script is attached and its entity is fully built
ScriptBehaviour.description:
**Not at attach time.** While a scene loads, components arrive one at a time, so a component you look for at attach time may not exist yet. By `OnStart` the entity is complete.

All five handles and every verb on `ScriptBehaviour` are valid from here onwards.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnFixedUpdate
ScriptBehaviour.summary: Every fixed simulation step. Movement, physics, anything timed
ScriptBehaviour.description:
Runs a whole number of times per drawn frame - sometimes twice, sometimes not at all - at a steady 1/60 s. That is what makes a game behave the same on every machine.

**It takes no delta.** Ask `Time::FixedDeltaTime()`. Writing `OnFixedUpdate(float dt)` is a compile error that says so rather than a hook that is silently never called.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnUpdate
ScriptBehaviour.summary: Once per drawn frame. Fades, menus, anything tied to the screen rather than the world
ScriptBehaviour.description:
Runs however often this machine happens to draw, so it is the wrong place for movement or physics - that is the whole reason the fixed step exists.

It is the right place for an **edge-triggered input read**. `InputMap::IsPressed` is true only on the frame the action went down, and input is sampled once per drawn frame - so asking in a fixed step can miss it entirely or see it twice. `IsHeld` and `IsDown` are level reads and work in either hook.

Ask `Time::DeltaTime()` here, or `Time::UnscaledDeltaTime()` for something that must keep moving while the game is paused. Like `OnFixedUpdate` it takes no argument.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnDestroy
ScriptBehaviour.summary: The entity is going away. Still safe to touch things here, and not afterwards
ScriptBehaviour.description: Runs at stage 600, when the queued destroy actually lands - not at the moment `Destroy` was called.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnCollisionEnter
ScriptBehaviour.signature: void OnCollisionEnter(eng::EntityId other) | void OnCollisionEnter(const eng::Collision2D& hit)
ScriptBehaviour.summary: A solid contact began - neither side is a trigger. Write whichever form you need
ScriptBehaviour.description:
**Two forms, and the richest one you write wins.** The contact form carries `hit.normal`, `hit.point` and `hit.relativeVelocity`, which is how landing on something is told from walking into it, plus `hit.thisCollider` - which of *your* colliders fired.

One event per collider **pair**: an entity with three colliders all touching the same wall gets three calls. Two colliders on the same entity never report each other.

An `EntityId` may already name something destroyed. Look it up through the scene every time.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnCollisionStay
ScriptBehaviour.signature: void OnCollisionStay(eng::EntityId other) | void OnCollisionStay(const eng::Collision2D& hit)
ScriptBehaviour.summary: Every step a solid contact continues
ScriptBehaviour.description: Fires once per step per pair for as long as the overlap lasts, in the same two forms as `OnCollisionEnter`.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnCollisionExit
ScriptBehaviour.signature: void OnCollisionExit(eng::EntityId other) | void OnCollisionExit(const eng::Collision2D& hit)
ScriptBehaviour.summary: A solid contact ended - including because the other entity was destroyed
ScriptBehaviour.description:
The pair has already ended by the time this arrives, so there is nothing left to point at: the exit forms take the id or the contact and never a bare collider.

It fires when the other entity is **destroyed** while still overlapping, as well as when it moves away, so a script can rely on seeing an exit for every enter.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnTriggerEnter
ScriptBehaviour.signature: void OnTriggerEnter(eng::EntityId other) | void OnTriggerEnter(Collider2D other) | void OnTriggerEnter(const eng::Collision2D& hit)
ScriptBehaviour.summary: An overlap began where either side has trigger ticked. Nothing is pushed apart
ScriptBehaviour.description:
**Three forms, and the richest one you write wins.** `Collider2D` is Unity's form and reaches the entity in one hop - `other->Owner()`. The contact form also says which of *your* colliders fired, as `hit.thisCollider`, which Unity cannot tell you at all.

**A pair sends collision events or trigger events, never both.** A script with `OnCollisionEnter` on a trigger collider is never called - and the engine reports that in the Console rather than leaving it silent. An entity carrying a trigger collider *and* a solid one gets both families at once, from the same pair.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnTriggerStay
ScriptBehaviour.signature: void OnTriggerStay(eng::EntityId other) | void OnTriggerStay(Collider2D other) | void OnTriggerStay(const eng::Collision2D& hit)
ScriptBehaviour.summary: Every step a trigger overlap continues
ScriptBehaviour.description: The same three forms as `OnTriggerEnter`, once per step per pair for as long as the overlap lasts.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnTriggerExit
ScriptBehaviour.signature: void OnTriggerExit(eng::EntityId other) | void OnTriggerExit(const eng::Collision2D& hit)
ScriptBehaviour.summary: A trigger overlap ended - including because the other entity was destroyed
ScriptBehaviour.description: Two forms, not three: the pair has already ended, so there is no collider left to hand you. Writing the collider form is a compile error that says exactly that.

ScriptBehaviour.name: OnExpose
ScriptBehaviour.summary: Lists this script's variables for the Inspector by hand. Not an event, and usually unnecessary
ScriptBehaviour.unity: no equivalent; Unity reflects over fields instead
ScriptBehaviour.description:
**You rarely need this.** A public variable of a supported type is already in the Inspector with no code at all - the editor reads the script's source when it builds it and generates the registration. Write `OnExpose` only when the set of controls has to be decided rather than declared.

Called **once**, when the script is bound - not every frame, and not when anything changes. A hand-written `OnExpose` is never overwritten by the generated one.

It is not a lifecycle hook: a script with `OnExpose` and nothing else never runs, and the registration macro says so at compile time.
